title: The robot API
description: One small object, a dozen or so methods — this is the entire vocabulary you'll use to program ARIA in real code.

content.value: Every Python exercise from here on gives you one ready-made object called robot, with a small, fixed set of methods. It mirrors the block palette from Module 9 almost exactly on purpose — you already know what every one of these does.

robot.forward(speed=50, seconds=0.3)   drive forward
robot.backward(speed=50, seconds=0.3)  drive backward
robot.left(degrees=90)                 turn left
robot.right(degrees=90)                turn right
robot.stop()                           stop
robot.wait(seconds=0.3)                pause
robot.distance()                       -> nearest obstacle, in simulated units
robot.line()                           -> (left_on_line, right_on_line)
robot.led(r, g, b)                     set an RGB LED
robot.say(text)                        speak a short message

Notice the shape of that list: some methods act (forward, left, stop) and some sense (distance, line) — the exact sense/act split from Module 1's very first lesson, now expressed as real function calls.

content.title: 🐍 Try a few calls
content.hint: This is a real, running simulation. Try robot.forward(60), then robot.left(90), then robot.forward(60) again.

content.value: Default values matter: robot.forward() with no arguments at all still runs, at speed 50 for 0.3 seconds, because every parameter above has a default. You only need to specify what you want to change.
Key takeaway: robot is a small, fixed API — a handful of act methods and a handful of sense methods, deliberately mirroring the block palette you already know.

quiz.question: Which of these robot methods senses the world rather than acting on it?
quiz.explain: distance() reports information back to your code; forward() and left() change the robot's physical state — sense vs act.

quiz.question: What does robot.forward() do if you call it with no arguments at all?
options: It raises an error, since arguments are required
It runs using its default speed and duration
quiz.explain: Every parameter has a default value, so calling it bare still does something sensible — speed 50 for 0.3 seconds.
